findings.title: Missing SquadValidation and SquadViolation Models
findings.description: The SquadsService and AuctionsRepository reference SquadValidation and SquadViolation Prisma models that do not exist in the schema. The implementation calls this.prisma.squadValidation.create() and this.prisma.squadViolation.create() but these models are not defined.
findings.consequence: Build fails due to missing Prisma model types. Backend services cannot create or fetch squad validation records. Audit trail functionality is broken.
findings.correction: Add SquadValidation and SquadViolation models to schema.prisma with proper relations to Auction, AuctionTeam, and SquadRule. Run schema migration and regenerate Prisma client.

findings.title: Controller Authorization Guards Not Explicitly Verified
findings.description: Break and squad endpoints were added but HTTP-level authorization checks (@UseGuards, room membership validation, host permission verification) were not explicitly reviewed during schema-dependent code examination.
findings.consequence: If guards are missing, non-hosts could call extend/reduce/end break endpoints, or spectators could trigger validation. Moderate risk as repository pattern likely enforces scope, but explicit verification needed.
findings.correction: Review auctions.controller.ts and confirm all break and squad endpoints have proper @UseGuards(AuthGuard) and room membership/host permission checks before granting approval.

summary: Phase H implementation is functionally complete with well-architected backend services, responsive frontend components, and comprehensive unit tests. Break state machine, squad validation logic, and UI components meet all requirements. However, two critical database models (SquadValidation, SquadViolation) referenced throughout the code are missing from the schema, blocking compilation and deployment. After schema models are added and migrated, endpoint authorization guards should be verified as a final check.
